lines.text: order to determine the most eﬀective method of uniformly increasing the temperature. Three
models were developed to describe this temperature distribution: a steady state uniform
model, an analytical heat equation model, and a numerical convection-diﬀusion equation
model. Ultimately, the numerical model proved most accurate because it alone took into
account bulk ﬂuid motion, the dominant heat transfer eﬀect. Using this model and the
analytical model, we conducted sensitivity analyses on diﬀerent parameters to explore the
eﬀects of diﬀerent bathtub geometries, the addition of soap, and other variations to the
problem at hand. We also implemented PID control of the inlet water temperature and
intelligent distribution of inlet water. By optimizing this process, we eﬀectively developed
a strategy for quickly re-heating the bath while maintaining uniformity. Overall, our model
showed that well-tuned PID control combined with distributing the inlet water upstream of
the bather proved to be the most eﬀective strategy.
